quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When turning left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, which lane should you start from?

options.text: Any lane (as long as it is safe).
The left lane, closest to the left curb.
The center lane of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane, closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: Start your left turn from the far left lane.

questions.question: A truck or bus is making a right turn where you also need to turn right. What should you do?

options.text: Turn quickly before the truck or bus does.
Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning, then turn.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning, then turn.
questions.explanation: Do not try to fit your car between a turning truck or bus and the curb. This causes serious crashes. Wait for the truck or bus to finish turning before you turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn left.
No left turn.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn left. Turning left here is unsafe and illegal.

questions.question: When must you yield to a pedestrian?

options.text: Only if they are in a crosswalk.
Always, even if they are not following traffic laws.
Only when traffic lights favor the pedestrian.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always, even if they are not following traffic laws.
questions.explanation: Always watch for pedestrians near your vehicle. Do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter what.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash.
When you drive faster, you need more space between you and the car ahead.
Both A and B.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds greatly increase the chance of death in a crash. At speeds over 80 mph, you have almost no chance of surviving a crash. You also need a longer distance to stop when driving faster, so increase the space between you and other cars as your speed increases.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Signal before going further.
Slow down and let trains pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let trains pass.
questions.explanation: A round sign warns of a railroad crossing ahead, usually a few hundred feet before the tracks. Slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does this white sign mean?

options.text: The crossing is controlled. Keep your regular speed.
Look, listen, and be ready to stop if needed.
Stop at the tracks and wait for a signal before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: At railroad crossings, look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop. Wait for any trains to pass before you go.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You must drive at this speed through the intersection.
The highest safe speed in good conditions is 55 mph.
You must not drive slower than this speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest safe speed in good conditions is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the speed limit. You can drive slower if road conditions require it, but you cannot drive faster than the posted limit.

questions.question: What does a steady red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: You cannot turn in that direction.
You can turn in that direction after you stop completely.
You can turn in that direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn in that direction.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means do not turn in that direction. You must stop and wait for a green signal.

questions.question: What should a driver do while driving?

options.text: Look straight ahead at the road in front.
Focus only on the center of the road.
Watch in front, beside, and behind your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch in front, beside, and behind your car.
questions.explanation: Watch all around your vehicle. Be aware of everything happening near your car.

questions.question: A large truck ahead of you is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. The truck:

options.text: May complete its turn in either of the two lanes.
May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.
Must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.
questions.explanation: When a vehicle turns, the rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels. Long trucks need extra space to turn right. They often swing wide to complete the turn safely.

questions.question: When driving in heavy fog, you should slow down and:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Turn your lights to high beam.
Turn your lights to low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your lights to low beam.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off water in the air and create glare, making it harder to see. Some cars have fog lights that should be used with low beams.

questions.question: When stopping on snow or ice in a car with Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you should:

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
Stay off the brakes and let the car slide to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
questions.explanation: With ABS, press the brake pedal hard and keep it pressed on snow or ice. The ABS automatically pumps the brakes faster than you could do it manually.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
U-turns are prohibited.
You may proceed if the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a one-way road or entrance. If you see this sign, traffic is coming toward you. Turn around and do not enter.

questions.question: After a train passes at a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Wait for signal lights to stop flashing.
Look for a second train.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: After a train passes, watch for a second train on any track. Do not proceed until all gates are raised and all warning lights stop flashing.

questions.question: What does this road sign indicate?

options.text: Directions for children
School zone ahead
Playground area ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: School zone ahead
questions.explanation: Pentagon-shaped signs warn you that you are near or entering a school zone or school crossing. Watch for children and follow the posted speed limits.

questions.question: Give the right-of-way to any pedestrian who is:

options.text: In a marked crosswalk.
In any crosswalk or intersection.
Crossing any street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossing any street.
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing in marked or unmarked crosswalks. For safety, yield to anyone crossing any street.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Hospital.
Upcoming intersection.
Railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Upcoming intersection.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and alert drivers to situations ahead. This sign warns of an upcoming intersection so you can prepare for traffic or turns.

questions.question: An orange-colored sign like this means:

options.text: There is roadwork ahead.
You must change lanes ahead.
There is a detour ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is roadwork ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs indicate construction areas. Drive with caution.

questions.question: This sign tells a driver that:

options.text: A construction flagger is ahead.
A police officer is ahead.
A parking attendant is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A construction flagger is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a flag person is ahead. Always follow their directions. Flaggers wear orange or yellow vests or bright jackets. They use paddles and flags to direct traffic through work zones.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights coming toward you, you must:

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane until it passes.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Pull to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it passes.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, pull to the right edge of the road and stop. Park parallel to the curb. On one-way streets, move toward the nearest road edge.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the roadway edge, you should:

options.text: Wait until it is safe, then slowly get back on the road.
Turn back onto the road right away.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until it is safe, then slowly get back on the road.
questions.explanation: If your wheels drop off the road edge, do not turn back right away. Slow down, check traffic, and turn back onto the road slowly when it is safe.

questions.question: To pass on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Check how far away oncoming vehicles are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check how far away oncoming vehicles are.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast oncoming vehicles are traveling. They may be coming faster than they appear. Always make sure you can safely change lanes before passing. If you are not sure about an oncoming vehicle's speed, wait until it has passed and there is enough space for you to change lanes safely.

questions.question: Which lane must you use before making a left turn from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane closest to the left curb.
The lane closest to the center of the street.
The lane closest to the right curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: When making a turn, turn from the lane closest to where you want to go into the first available legal lane. For a left turn from a one-way street, use the lane nearest the left curb.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Yield the right-of-way.
No passing zone.
Fewer lanes ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A triangular red and white sign means you must yield the right-of-way.

questions.question: Using a cell phone while driving is a distraction because:

options.text: It makes you worry about the call cost.
It takes your hands, eyes, and mind off driving.
It gets the attention of other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes your hands, eyes, and mind off driving.
questions.explanation: Using a cell phone while driving is dangerous because it takes your eyes, hands, and mind away from the road. Even skilled drivers increase their crash risk by using a cell phone while driving.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The road gets wider ahead.
One lane is ending soon. Move left to merge with other traffic.
A highway entrance ramp is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: One lane is ending soon. Move left to merge with other traffic.
questions.explanation: A warning sign is usually yellow with black marks. This sign warns that lanes ahead are being reduced and traffic must merge to the left.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Change lanes suddenly without warning.
Check for other vehicles in the lane you want to enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes suddenly without warning.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, make sure no vehicles are in your way. Check your mirrors and blind spots. Always use your turn signal before changing lanes to warn other drivers.

questions.question: If the rear of your vehicle skids to the left, you should:

options.text: Do not turn your steering wheel.
Turn your steering wheel to the left to stop the skid.
Turn your steering wheel to the right to stop the skid.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel to the left to stop the skid.
questions.explanation: If you skid on a wet or icy road, take your foot off the gas, do not brake, and turn your wheel in the direction of the skid. If you have anti-lock brakes, press the brakes hard and steer straight ahead.

questions.question: If your vehicle breaks down, you should:

options.text: Signal and move to the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and turn on your hazard lights.
Turn on your hazard lights and pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your hazard lights and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down on a highway, make sure other drivers can see it. Get your vehicle off the road and away from traffic if possible and turn on your emergency lights to show you are having trouble.
